eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket closely splits between 26°C and 27°C as the highest temperature in Mexico City on May 3, reflecting uncertainty in short-range forecasts from the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN). Latest SMN guidance indicates May 2 highs of 27-29°C amid a lingering heat wave, but the advancing Frente Frío 48 and its associated polar air mass are poised to introduce chubascos (5-25 mm rain) and cloud cover over the Valle de México, potentially capping diurnal heating and favoring 26°C. Climatological averages for early May hover at 26.3°C, bolstered by Mexico City's 2,240-meter elevation, though 2026 seasonal outlooks predict 2-3°C above normal due to persistent anticyclonic circulation. Key differentiators include model divergence on moisture timing and upper-level trough strength; daily SMN updates and GFS/ECMWF ensembles through May 2 will refine this.
